adversarial_test_results.prompt: The dog chased the ball across the yard, and the tired dog brought it straight back to us.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Repeated/given-word control: the second 'dog' is the same content word given again, so the hypothesis predicts low activation despite the first 'dog' being a claimed activator.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It is what it is, and it will be what it will be, as it always was.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Pure predictable-function-word sentence with no least-predictable new content, so the graded-novelty hypothesis predicts low activation throughout.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The orchestra tuned their instruments before the symphony began, and the symphony then played on exactly as everyone expected.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Keeps the 'symphony' trigger token but as a repeated, fully predictable second mention after the identical clause from the top example, so the hypothesis predicts low activation on it.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I am here with you now.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Sentence-final period after a trivial, fully predictable clause with no novel content, testing the claim that the period response summarizes a novel clause.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The odometer clicked from 98 to 99 to 100 to 101 exactly as expected.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Keeps the number trigger '100' but in a fully predictable counting sequence and without its attribution driver 'boils', so the novelty hypothesis predicts no activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The old telescope sat in the shed, and the dusty telescope stayed in the shed all winter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same telescope topic and vocabulary as a top example but with only repeated, given content and no new disambiguating token, so the hypothesis predicts low activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: October comes after September, just as October always comes after September every single year.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Date trigger 'October' in a tautological, fully predictable and repeated context, testing whether the neuron fires on the date token itself or only on unpredictable dates.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Please turn the light on, and then please turn that same light right back off again.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Trigger token 'light' as a repeated, given referent in a predictable on/off collocation, so the first-mention novelty hypothesis predicts low activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Yes. No. Fine. OK. Sure.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Delimiter-only control with sentence-final periods but zero novel clausal content, testing the massive-activation/delimiter confound for the claimed period response.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: River told River that River would meet River after class as planned.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Unpredictable-name trigger 'River' repeated until fully given, testing the claim that unpredictable names fire only on first mention.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The quarterly planning meeting opened with a review of the previous meeting. The chair of the meeting read the minutes of the last meeting aloud to the meeting. Every member of the meeting nodded, because every meeting follows the same agenda as the meeting before. The first item of the meeting was the budget, which the meeting had already approved at the prior meeting. The second item of the meeting was staffing, which the meeting had already discussed at the earlier meeting. The third item of the meeting was scheduling, and the meeting agreed to hold the next meeting on the same day as every meeting before it. The chair thanked the meeting for attending the meeting and reminded the meeting that the meeting exists to repeat the work of each meeting. The members of the meeting then reviewed the notes from the last meeting, confirmed the notes of this meeting matched the notes of the previous meeting, and filed them with the records of every meeting on file. Old business at the meeting was the same old business as the last meeting. New business at the meeting was the same new business as the last meeting. The chair asked whether any member of the meeting had anything new to bring to the meeting, and no member of the meeting spoke, since nothing at this meeting differed from the prior meeting. The chair then summarized the meeting by repeating the summary of the previous meeting almost word for word to the current meeting. With nothing further to add, the meeting simply continued as the same meeting it had always been, closing this meeting exactly the way the last meeting had closed, with the next meeting already scheduled to repeat the meeting all over again.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long-context givenness control: the content word 'meeting' is repeated dozens of times across a long passage, so by the final clause it is fully given and the hypothesis predicts low activation despite the long retrospective context.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The mechanic rebuilt the cracked carburetor while the apprentice fetched a torque wrench.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel holdout with rare-word disambiguating content ('carburetor', 'torque') in a garage domain unlike any top example, predicted to fire on the least predictable new token.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Ambassador Kielsen landed in Reykjavik on February 29 carrying forty-seven crates of salted cod.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel holdout combining an unpredictable name, date, and number/unit ('Kielsen', 'February 29', 'forty-seven crates') in fresh wording, all classes the hypothesis says drive peaks.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Fold the sourdough gently and let the fermentation continue undisturbed overnight.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Cross-dataset holdout from the recipe/instruction genre with first-mentioned rare content words ('sourdough', 'fermentation') absent from the scan examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The beekeeper pulled wild honey from a hollow oak before sunrise.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel clause of first-mentioned content words ('beekeeper', 'hollow oak') ending in a sentence-final period, testing the claimed moderate period response after genuinely new content.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The audit revealed a shortfall of 8,412 pesos owed to a merchant named Valdez.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Finance-ledger genre holdout expressing unpredictable number and name ('8,412 pesos', 'Valdez') with tokens absent from the top examples, beating the trigger-token baseline.
